role: the unmeasured library a request is screened against. No labels: ZINC22 carries no measurements, so nothing here is fitted on it
why_this_manifest_exists: the ingested parquet recorded its source as a path in a session temporary directory, which no longer exists. Every ZINC figure in docs/HANDOFF.md came from these slices, and until this file was written there was nothing that said which tranche they were. The identifier is the whole content: with it anyone can fetch the same bytes, and without it the measurements cannot be re-derived by anyone, including this project after a reboot

source.verified_from: data/raw/_searched.json, entry "ZINC22 (files.docking.org, tranche-level SMILES)", checked_here: true

format.header: none. The first line is already a molecule; a reader that skips it loses one
format.charge_suffix_note: this is the PREDICTED PROTONATION STATE, not the formal charge of the written structure. Nearly every SMILES in every slice is written in neutral form. The two quantities were confused once, and the charge knob was retired for it; see knobs.RETIRED['charge'] and py/charge_slices.py

slices_ingested.note: exactly 1,000,000 is a truncation, not the size of the slice. The slice is larger and was cut at a round number; nothing here records the full count, so do not read 1,000,000 as the slice size
the slice this project screens. Richter et al. 2017 associate a positive charge with accumulation, so this is the slice their data points at
small, and the richest in primary amines. Used for trial runs
never ingested. A partial download of it was measured once by py/charge_slices.py, from a pool of its first 80,000 molecules. Any figure about -M describes that prefix, not the slice

filenames.keep_them: the generation letter sits between the charge suffix and .smi.gz. The local copies were renamed to x_H29P240-<charge>.smi.gz, moving the generation letter to the front, and the provenance reader that exists to recover the slice stopped working on its own project's files. Contraindication 67. Fetch to the canonical name

licence.summary: ZINC's terms require written permission from John Irwin to redistribute large portions, and explicitly permit screening and sharing screening results. No commercial restriction clause
licence.consequence: screening without redistributing the library is in scope

not_retained.what: the raw .smi.gz tranches are not in this repository and no SHA256SUMS is recorded for them
not_retained.why: a deliberate licence decision, not an oversight: redistributing large portions needs written permission, so the tranches are kept out
not_retained.cost: the bytes cannot be checksummed against what was ingested. This manifest fixes the identity of what to fetch, which is the most that can be fixed without keeping the files
not_retained.what_would_close_it: record the server's ETag or Content-Length per slice at fetch time, which identifies the bytes without redistributing them

generations_not_used.which: n, and the 2d/ and 2d-all/ paths, which return 401
generations_not_used.why: the site publishes credentials for the protected generations as a riddle. They were NOT used. The site states the protection exists to keep never-been-made molecules off the open internet so that composition-of-matter patentability is preserved, so drawing candidates from them could affect the patentability of anything published from them. That is the project owner's decision, not a technical one. The open generations supply the needed mass range and scale, so nothing here depends on it

evidence.why: a library to screen, not evidence to answer from. ZINC22 is unmeasured: it carries no label, so a target question put to it could only ever return nothing. Listing it as evidence would say a question had been asked of it.

fetch.why_optional: ZINC22's terms permit screening and the sharing of screening results and require written permission to redistribute large portions. Nothing here redistributes it; this fetches it from the source, which is the reader's own download. It is opt-in because it is the only large one and because every request naming CHAMP, IMI, GramNegAccum or B3DB works without it.
fetch.no_checksum: NO CHECKSUM IS RECORDED FOR ANY SLICE, so a fetch of these cannot be verified the way the other four are. What is checked instead is the row count after ingest, against rows_ingested below. That is weaker: it would not notice a slice whose contents changed without changing length. Said here rather than left to be assumed.
not_fetched: the -M slice: never ingested, and no figure in this repository rests on more than a prefix of it
